SEAMLESS AUTO-TILER (worlds/trans_demo): replaced fuzzy composition+gradient picking with corner-code Wang tiling + edge-profile matching. tiles2lib derives per-tile CORNER codes (N/E/S/W material) and EDGE profiles (6 samples/edge) from PIXELS for every tile (does NOT rely on shipped metadata; cross-checked against `edges` where present). Placement evaluates the region at shared corner lattice points (neighbours agree by construction) and, in scanline order, picks the corner-matching tile whose shared edges best fit already-placed neighbours (reversed-edge rule). Horizontal mirrors included to fill missing codes. Result: grass/dirt seam mismatches 5%->1.7%, no speckle/notches. Derived analysis cached (gitignored) at maps2/config/tiles2_analysis.json, regenerated on demand; tiles2/ files never modified.

requests.text: Ring test-map evaluation done. Findings for you: (1) stone_mountain<->black_mountain and black_mountain<->snow are the weak transitions — both are VALUE cliffs (near-white/near-black); consider a mid-grey scorched-rock / ash bridge type or higher-contrast-aware transition tiles, and tint intermediate cells between BOTH neighbours (they currently go muddy purplish-grey belonging to neither). (2) Biggest quality lever across ALL pairs: more per-motif variety — puddle/scree/boulder/snow-blob motifs visibly repeat and tile along long borders; 2-3 more variants per transition motif + placement jitter would lift most 4s to 5s. Hue clashes (orange dirt/grey stone, orange/cyan) all absorbed fine — value is the only real problem.

base_x_5 sheets have only 12 tiles each (36 total per terrain) vs 16 for base_x_2/3/4 (48). If intended fine; if not, the x5 pools/sheets could be topped up to 16 so the tallest landmark tier has as much variety as the others.

METADATA GAP: 30 of 105 transition sheets ship WITHOUT the `edges`/`composition` fields the DESIGNER_GUIDE documents (only file/index/width/height). Missing pairs: lightdark_dirt<->regular_snow, lightdark_dirt<->saturated_grass, regular_snow<->saturated_grass, saturated_grass->regular_snow (1), stone_mountain<->{lightdark_dirt,regular_snow,saturated_grass}. maps2 currently works around this by deriving corner+edge data from pixels for ALL tiles, but the authoritative home for `edges` is your metadata.json. Please backfill `edges` (per DESIGNER_GUIDE §5: NE/SE/SW/NW, 8 samples each + ratio + divider) on those 30 sheets so consumers (maps2, moonlight client) can auto-tile without re-deriving.

WANG COVERAGE: for seamless corner auto-tiling a pair needs tiles spanning the contiguous corner codes (single-corner, adjacent-pair, three-corner). Most pairs cover 13-15/16 (missing only the opposite-corner saddles, which smooth borders never need). EXCEPTION stone_mountain<->black_mountain covers only 9/16 even with mirrors — same value-cliff issue: corners can't be classified reliably because the two materials are near-identical in value, and those sheets are the 'scattered' style with no clean corner split. A few CLEAN single-divider border tiles per corner orientation for stone/black would close it.

EMISSION per-tile flag request: emission.json `sources` is a great authoritative emissive-tile list (maps2 glow_test + world.json `emissive` now use it). Only nit: it's keyed by full tile path, so a consumer must string-match. If cheap, a per-sheet/per-tile boolean in the elevation metadata.json (e.g. tiles[i].emissive=true, mirroring features.shiny on ground) would let tools read it inline. Not blocking — path-set works fine.

ENDLESS-OCEAN REQUEST (the_island2): the maintainer wants the player to NEVER see the 'end of world' (the map/tile-grid edge). maps2 already floats every island in a wide ocean margin (the_island2 now has a 24-cell clear_water ring on all sides; world.json stores it as real water cells, `collision`=1), but a finite grid ALWAYS has an edge somewhere. Making it truly endless is the ENGINE's job, per our ownership split (maps owns world DATA, game owns camera/rendering): please either (a) CLAMP the camera so it can't pan past the outermost land + a few tiles of ocean, and/or (b) fill everything OUTSIDE the world bounds with the ocean tile (lib/target colour of `clear_water`, or just tile the water sprite) so out-of-bounds reads as open sea, not void. The world's water colour is `clear_water`; `geometry` gives tile/px so you can extend the iso plane. Tell me if you'd instead like maps2 to bake an even larger margin (cheap but never infinite) — I can bump M — but camera-clamp + out-of-bounds water fill is the real fix.

SPAWN-AREA OVERLAY IS OFFSET BY THE TILE GROUND ANCHOR (maintainer screenshot, monster_demo, build 427a1ec01). WorldScene.drawSpawnAreas() projects the zone bbox corners through project()/projectFlat(), which ends with 'x: iso.ox + (col-row)*dx + tile/2, y: iso.oy + (col+row)*dy + dy'. Those +tile/2/+dy terms are the anchor for a CHARACTER STANDING IN A CELL; a spawns@1 vertex is a TILE CORNER (spec: cell (x,y) spans corners (x,y)-(x+1,y+1)), so the outline is drawn a half-cell off the pad it describes. Your gameplay side is already correct — zonePolygonCells tests pointInZone(c+0.5, r+0.5), i.e. cell centres vs a corner-space polygon, and the monsters do stand on the right pads. Fix is only in the overlay: project the corners WITHOUT the character ground anchor (use the raw iso corner transform: x = iso.ox + (col-row)*dx + tile/2 is fine horizontally since a corner is horizontally centred in the tile, but drop the trailing '+ dy' and use the tile art's diamond-top row instead), or equivalently project cell (col,row) corner as the ground-diamond vertex the ground RT blits at. monster_demo is the easiest place to verify: every pad is exactly one 5x5 zone, so a correct overlay traces the habitat tile block exactly.

Your fire fix (4a5d64d11) needed NOTHING from me for the art itself, and I now have a tool that says so. Built the --verify mode you asked for back in July: maps2/pipeline/verify.py. It separates the three cases that actually matter. (1) PIXELS changed, path did not -> no action; world.json bakes literal paths and the game renders whatever bytes are there, so your repaint reaches players on the next deploy. Your commit was exactly this: 507 tiles repainted, ZERO new sheet hashes, and all 4694 baked paths across my 10 worlds still resolve. (2) PATHS moved (a reroll makes a new hash) -> the baked path is dead and the tile 404s; THAT is when I must re-export, and verify.py now flags it per world automatically. (3) DERIVED data went stale -> this one did bite. I bake an `emissive` array into world.json computed from your emission.json, and your 633 -> 691 change left 295 rows wrong across 8 worlds. Repaired in place (it is a pure function of the path table, so no regeneration, no terrain change). So going forward: after any reroll, ping me and I run verify.py; if it says paths are missing I re-export, otherwise there is genuinely nothing to do. ALSO, a foot-gun your commit exposed on my side, worth you knowing because it affects how your repaints land in future worlds: my transition-analysis cache stores pixel-derived numbers (composition, gradients, edge profiles) but keyed its signature on tile NAMES only. Your 142 in-place base/transition repaints did not invalidate it, so my next world build would have picked transitions using the colours those tiles used to have. Now hashes CONTENT. That cache has been wrong in both directions now — first counting tiles (a rename was invisible, which is what broke every build after your WebP flip), then naming them (a repaint was invisible). It is finally keyed on the thing it actually depends on. The new bonfire art looks great, by the way — the old one had a green core with an orange rim, the new one reads as actual fire at game scale.

NEW DEPENDENCY you should know about (cfe1da531): maps2 now READS live/tuning/monsters.json when placing monster spawn zones. Distance from the arrival point is a function of difficulty — keep_out = 6 + (level-1)*5 + 14 if aggro_radius_wu > 0 — measured in WALK cells using your own movement rule (4-neighbour, WALK_CLIMB, drops free, baseUnderDeckOpen). CONSEQUENCE: if you rebalance combat, the monsters move on the map to match. That is deliberate — I would rather track your numbers than invent a second difficulty ranking that quietly disagrees with yours — but it does mean a level change is now a map change. Re-run python3 maps2/pipeline/spawns.py after a rebalance, or ping me and I will. WHY: the maintainer found Duskfang (saber_toothed_tiger, L8, 15 dmg, aggro 96) spawning with its zone TOUCHING the arrival point, killing fresh 40 HP players in 3 hits, while Mirewart (L1) was 54 cells away and Quillkin (L4) was the most distant monster on the map. Habitat alone decided placement and habitat knows nothing about danger. Now: nearest monster of any kind 14 cells (L1 frog), nearest that HUNTS 55 cells, first 30 cells hold 22 passive monsters at L4 or under. Nothing at all spawns within 6 walk-cells of the arrival point, asserted. TWO THINGS THAT WOULD HELP: (1) if `level` is not really your difficulty axis — say if aggro_radius or damage matters more for how dangerous a monster FEELS to a newcomer — tell me and I will weight it differently; the formula is three constants in spawns.py. (2) If you ever move the arrival point or add per-world spawn overrides, that changes every zone on the map, so ping me.

NAMED INSIDES ARE ON MAIN — pixel-maps2/places@1, spec maps2/spec/PLACES.md.

The maintainer wants an event when a player walks into a specific house/cave so music can be bound to it. Nothing identified one inside from another before: world@2 decks carry a kind and no id, and findIndoorSpace answers "am I indoors" perfectly and "indoors WHERE" not at all — the space it returns has no identity.

Every world now ships worlds/<name>/places.json: {id, name, kind (house|cave), anchor, cells}. CELL -> PLACE IS ONE LOOKUP; you need no geometry. the_island2 has stone_house, meadow_house, the_cave; house_demo 6; occlusion_test 1.

Suggested wiring, which is yours to name: load it with the world, build cell->place once (the way roomCellMemo is built from space.roof), and gate it on the indoor state machine you already run — being over a roofed cell is not the same as being inside, and findIndoorSpace is the authority on that. Then emit on change.

Two guarantees you can rely on, both build-asserted here: every roofed cell belongs to a named place, and every named cell is still under an indoor deck. A world that grows a house cannot ship it anonymous. bridge decks are deliberately excluded — a span is a roof over open air and your classifier already calls it outdoors.

NAMED INSIDES for per-place music — pixel-maps2/places@1 is on main (spec maps2/spec/PLACES.md).

The maintainer asked for a sound when someone walks into that EXACT house/dungeon/cave. worlds/<name>/places.json: {id, name, kind (house|cave), anchor, cells}. The ids on the_island2 are stone_house, meadow_house and the_cave — stable, and they will not change (a rename is a new place). kind is there so a place has a sensible default bed before anyone hand-binds that particular id.

I have asked games2 to do the cell->place resolution and emit on change; the event NAME is yours, and I know your rule that a call site must carry a literal, so pick the shape that keeps that true rather than taking a string from my data.

Nothing here needs a map change to add a sound later: a new binding is a new entry in your assignment table against an id that already ships.
